source: Sayari Graph trade search facets (bills of lading and customs records), retrieved via the Sayari MCP connector
note: Shipment-record counts by departure country, all years Sayari holds. Hand-entered from search_trade_facets; no company is named. Departure country is the country a shipment left from, which is not always where the goods were made.

input.label: Solar cells
input.suspect: Kenya and Nigeria appear as departure countries but never as product origin, so treat them as possible record errors.

solar.gist: Most cells reach Indonesia’s module plants from China, so the duty question is how much assembly happens in Indonesia.
solar.check: Compare cell imports with module exports, and ask module makers where their cells and wafers were made.

aluminum.gist: Canada’s smelters rely largely on imported alumina, which in Sayari’s records ships mostly from India and Brazil.
aluminum.check: Check the smelt-and-cast country, which U.S. importers must report for aluminum, against the mill certificate.

cotton.gist: India grows most of its own cotton; these imports top it up, led by Australia and the U.S.
cotton.check: Ask for fiber-origin records back to the gin, since imported and domestic cotton mix at the spinning mill.

seafood.gist: India’s shrimp is farmed at home; one imported input is feed, which in these records ships mostly from Vietnam. The code also covers other animal feed.
seafood.check: Trace the farms and processing plants behind each exporter; labor risk sits there more than on the feed route.

honey.gist: India’s honey imports are small next to its exports (about 700 records in, 8,578 out to the U.S.), and China is not among the top departure countries.
honey.check: Compare export volumes with India’s hive output, and test for blending; origin fraud rarely shows in shipping records.

gold.gist: These records lean to Latin America because those countries publish shipment-level customs data; gold that moves by air is largely missing.
gold.check: Ask refiners for mine-of-origin and LBMA audit reports; shipping records cover only part of the gold that arrives.

tin.domestic: Tin ore is mined and smelted in Bolivia itself; Sayari holds no imported tin ore into Bolivia.
tin.gist: This chain stays inside Bolivia until the metal ships, so the risk sits at the mine.
tin.check: Ask for smelter and mine names and check them against the RMI conformant smelter list.

timber.domestic: Logs are harvested in Brazil and sawn there before export.

elsewhere.label: Other buyers of Brazil’s sawn tropical timber

timber.gist: Brazil saws its own logs; the U.S. is the second-largest buyer in these records, after the Netherlands.
timber.check: Match species and volumes against harvest permits; the legality risk sits at the forest, not at sea.
